tests.title: GET /api/watchlist/ lists the user's movies in the order added
Adding saves the entry; a duplicate gets 400
Removing deletes the entry; a missing one gets 404
The status check returns true or false
Add: missing, malformed and unknown movie ids
Each user has their own watchlist
Failed requests count toward the limit
Reading the watchlist isn't rate limited

bugs.why: get_watchlist calls Watchlist.objects.for_user(), which doesn't exist, so the list always fails with 500
bugs.fix: Query the user's entries in the order they were added: Watchlist.objects.filter(user=request.user).select_related("movie").order_by("created_at", "id").

edits.fixed:
entries = Watchlist.objects.filter(user=request.user).select_related("movie").order_by("created_at", "id")
        movies = [entry.movie for entry in entries]
edits.buggy:
entries = Watchlist.objects.for_user(request.user)
        movies = [entry.movie for entry in entries if entry.movie]

bugs.why: add_to_watchlist builds a Watchlist object but never saves it, and never checks for duplicates
bugs.fix: Answer 400 "Movie already in watchlist" when the entry exists, otherwise Watchlist.objects.create(...). The unique constraint and the IntegrityError branch are only a safety net.

bugs.why: remove_from_watchlist builds a query but never deletes anything, and never answers 404
bugs.fix: deleted, _ = Watchlist.objects.filter(user=request.user, movie_id=movie_id).delete(), then 404 "Movie not found in watchlist" when nothing was deleted.

bugs.why: check_watchlist_status returns a list of rows instead of true / false
the remove route points at the add view, so POST /api/watchlist/remove adds the movie again
the rate limiter keeps the expired timestamps (>= instead of <), so recent requests are never counted and nobody is limited
bugs.fix: Keep the timestamps with current - stamp < WINDOW_SECONDS.
